note.note:
History:
- Presenting complaint: acute vertigo and nausea.
- Onset/duration: began approximately 2 hours prior to consultation while making breakfast; continuous since onset.
- Symptoms/progression: room feels like it is spinning (rotatory vertigo), persistent unsteadiness (can walk but not straight), buzzing in both ears, nauseous (no vomiting), similar but shorter episode ~1 month ago lasting ~5–10 minutes that resolved spontaneously.
- Associated/negative features: no ear pain or ear discharge, no reported hearing loss (hearing otherwise intact), no recent viral illness, no reported fever, no weakness of arms or legs.

Past Medical History:
- Premature ovarian failure; patient reports taking hormone replacement therapy (HRT) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- No other chronic medical or surgical history disclosed.
- Medications: HRT only (dose/route/frequency not documented); patient stated "no" to other medications.
- Allergies: none reported.

Physical Examination:
- Reported/observed findings during consult:
  - Persistent vertigo with subjective spinning sensation.
  - Unsteady gait reported; limbs reportedly moving normally.
  - Ear buzzing (tinnitus) without pain or discharge.
  - Nausea without vomiting.
  - No focal limb weakness reported.
- Examination limitations: clinician noted inability to see patient's face clearly on video; no documented ear inspection, blood pressure, or formal neurological/gait exam performed during this encounter.

Impression:
- Probable labyrinthitis causing acute vertigo and tinnitus.

Management Plan:
- Symptomatic medication prescribed (name not documented); prescribed as one tablet three times a day for approximately 10 days — medication name and route not documented.
- Prescription sent to Lloyd pharmacy per system.
- Advise patient to be seen in-person by clinic physician for ear examination, blood pressure measurement, and assessment of gait/neurological status in the next few days.
- Safety advice given: attend A&E urgently if new weakness of arms/legs, sudden severe headache, or if patient becomes violently vomitous.
- Advice regarding medication administration: may take tablets with or without food as tolerated.
- Patient advised to call support to book the follow-up appointment.

Patient Summary:
- Patient presented with sudden-onset, continuous rotatory vertigo, tinnitus, and nausea beginning ~2 hours prior while at home. Clinical impression is probable labyrinthitis. A symptomatic medication course was prescribed and an in-person review with examination (ears, BP, gait) has been arranged/advised.

Key Takeaways:
- Take the prescribed medication as directed (one tablet three times daily for ~10 days); verify specifics with pharmacist/clinic since medication name not documented.
- Arrange and attend in-person review for ear examination, blood pressure check, and neurological/gait assessment.
- Seek immediate emergency care if new weakness, severe headache, or uncontrollable vomiting develops.

Next Steps:
- Patient to contact support to book in-person appointment with clinic physician within next few days.
- In-person assessment to include otoscopic ear exam, blood pressure, focused neurological and gait examination.
- Pharmacy to dispense prescribed medication (verify name, route, and any contraindications with pharmacist).

Quality checks:
- Missing/expected elements not documented: medication name; medication route explicitly not documented; vital signs (blood pressure, heart rate, temperature); formal neurological exam findings; otoscopic ear exam findings; duration/dose/frequency of HRT; exact timing of follow-up appointment.
- Internal conflicts: clinician incorrectly stated "charting premature hearing failure" when patient reported premature ovarian failure — conflict noted.
- Transcript quality: overall audible but with some brief inaudible/ellided segments and occasional transcription errors; limited video visualization noted by clinician (face not clearly seen), and several clinical examination elements were not performed/documented during this consult.
